title: Lotus Temple
tagline: Lotus Temple — Pure White Marble Baháʼí Temple of Peace & Unity

heroImage.alt: Lotus Temple iconic view in Delhi, India

overview.short: Lotus Temple in South Delhi is an internationally acclaimed Baháʼí House of Worship renowned for its flower-like 27 pure white marble petals.
overview.description: Completed in 1986 by Iranian-Canadian architect Fariborz Sahba, the Lotus Temple is shaped like a blossoming sacred lotus flower with 27 free-standing petals crafted from Greek Penteli white marble. Welcoming people of all faiths, its central hall accommodates 2,500 visitors surrounded by nine serene blue ponds and 26 acres of verdant landscaped gardens.
overview.about: The Lotus Temple has won numerous international architectural accolades and stands as one of the most visited buildings in the world. It serves as a space for silent meditation and universal reflection where scriptures of all world religions may be read.

howToReach.roadNote: Located adjacent to Kalkaji Mandir Metro Station (interchange for Magenta and Violet Lines). Excellent connectivity via Outer Ring Road.

routes.byTrain: Magenta Line Metro direct to Kalkaji Mandir

routes.via: Mathura Road & Lala Lajpat Rai Marg

faq.q: What is the entry fee for Lotus Temple?
faq.a: Entry to Lotus Temple is completely free for all visitors regardless of nationality or faith.

faq.q: Which metro station is nearest to Lotus Temple?
faq.a: Kalkaji Mandir Metro Station (Magenta & Violet Lines interchange) is just 300 metres from the entrance gate.

faq.q: Is photography allowed inside the Lotus Temple?
faq.a: Photography is allowed in the gardens and exterior, but strictly prohibited inside the main prayer hall to maintain silence and sanctity.

faq.q: What are the visiting hours for Lotus Temple?
faq.a: Open from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM (winter) / 6:00 PM (summer), closed on Mondays.
